issue.title: epic(architecture): enforce state, layering, and dependency boundaries
issue.body:
## Summary

The app still has too many places where UI, service, repository, and state-management boundaries are blurred. We have enough concrete examples now that this should be tracked as one coordinated architecture epic instead of many disconnected audit leaves.

This issue is the source of truth for architecture work focused on layering, dependency direction, and state ownership.

## Problem

Current problems include:
- UI layers depending on services directly instead of going through BLoC/Cubit or repository boundaries
- inconsistent state-management patterns across features
- weak dependency direction between screens, services, repositories, and clients
- feature code spread across cross-cutting folders without a stable ownership model
- long-lived structural debt that makes fixes harder to sequence cleanly

## Scope

- enforce UI -> BLoC/Cubit -> Repository -> Client boundaries
- reduce direct service usage from widgets and screens
- clarify state ownership and migration direction
- improve feature/module organization where it materially reduces churn
- move toward constructor-injected dependencies over global/singleton reach-through

## Existing Related Work

- `#3620`
- `#3621`
- `#3622`
- `#3623`
- `#3625`
- `#3626`
- `#3627`
- `#3619`
- `#3617`

## Acceptance Criteria

- architecture cleanup is tracked through a coherent parent issue instead of scattered audit leaves
- boundary violations are grouped into executable child work where appropriate
- dependency direction expectations are explicit enough to guide future PRs
- related leaf audit issues can be closed or superseded into this epic

## Done When

- the app has a clearer and more defensible layering model
- new work no longer needs to rediscover the same architecture problems independently
- the highest-value architecture fixes are decomposed into clear execution issues

---

## Assignee
`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. define boundary rules and execution slices
2. group and supersede overlapping audit leaves
3. execute the highest-value structural fixes first

## Subgroup
- `@NotThatKindOfDrLiz` — DRI
- `@realmeylisdev` — state/routing support
- `@untreu2` — implementation support

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when an architecture decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this issue as the coordination source of truth for architecture boundary cleanup
- prefer reducing future churn over narrow local cleanup
- avoid “papering over” boundary violations with helpers if dependency direction remains wrong
- split implementation into concrete children when work becomes execution-ready

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.

issue.title: ci(architecture): ratchet UI imports of the service layer

labels.name: architecture
labels.description: Layer violations, dependency direction, and project organization

issue.body:
## Description

First executable slice of architecture epic **#4338** (Wave 0 — *stop the regression before migrating*).

`.claude/rules/architecture.md` requires the presentation layer to reach data through `UI → BLoC/Cubit → Repository → Client`. Today **96** files under `lib/screens/` and `lib/widgets/` still import `package:openvine/services/…` directly, bypassing BLoC — and that count has been *growing* because nothing enforces the rule (only `check_riverpod_boundary.sh` is wired to CI; `custom_lint`/`riverpod_lint` are disabled by an rxdart `^0.28.0` conflict).

This adds a **shell-based ratchet** mirroring the existing guard precedent (`check_riverpod_boundary.sh`, `check_raw_logging.sh`):

- `mobile/scripts/check_ui_service_boundary.sh` — fails CI when a screen/widget **not in the baseline** adds a direct `package:openvine/services/` import, and when a **baselined file no longer imports services** (so wins get locked in). The baseline may only ever shrink.
- `mobile/scripts/baseline/ui_service_imports.txt` — the 96 pre-existing violators, frozen. Regenerate with `UPDATE_BASELINE=1 bash mobile/scripts/check_ui_service_boundary.sh`. Intentional exceptions take a trailing `# reason`.
- Wired as a step in the `generated-files` CI job.
- Documented in `docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md` (new "CI Enforcement (ratchets)" section).

This does **not** fix any of the 96 violators — it freezes them and prevents new ones. Violators are removed from the baseline as later epic slices migrate each screen/widget onto a BLoC.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #4338

## Out of Scope

- UI under `lib/features/**` (only 4 files today) — scoped to `screens/`+`widgets/` for now; fast-follow widens it.
- Relative-import detection (`../../services/x.dart`) — the codebase uses `package:` imports overwhelmingly (very_good_analysis prefers them).
- A `ChangeNotifier` ratchet (baseline 15) and a `build()`-transform guard — fast-follow, same mechanism.
- Fixing the 96 baselined violators — that is the Wave-2 migration work, one feature at a time.

## Verification

- `bash -n` syntax check + `shellcheck` (only SC2001 style, identical to the existing `check_raw_logging.sh` precedent; shellcheck is not in CI).
- Guard self-tests: clean tree → exit 0; a new violating widget → exit 1 naming the file; a stale baseline entry → exit 1 instructing baseline regeneration. Artifacts cleaned up.
- Baseline generated by the guard's own `UPDATE_BASELINE=1` path → exactly 96 entries; re-verify green.
- `LC_ALL=C` forces byte-wise ordering so `sort`/`comm` agree between macOS (local) and Linux (CI).
- Workflow YAML validated (parses; new step present in `generated-files`).
- No Dart changed, so `flutter analyze`/tests are unaffected.

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [x] ✅ Build configuration change
- [x] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

issue.title: fix(notifications): unify push, local, and in-app tap routing (#4727)
issue.body:
## Description

Unifies the three notification tap entry points — FCM system push
(`getInitialMessage` / `onMessageOpenedApp`), local-notification taps, and
in-app notification rows — behind **one shared routing decision**,
`resolveNotificationTapTarget` (new, pure, Flutter-free). They can no longer
drift on where a tap lands, whether comments auto-open, or how unresolved
targets fall back. Each path keeps its own navigation mechanics/UX (the in-app
path keeps its `PooledFullscreenVideoFeedScreen` + snackbar behavior).

Fixes grounded in the `divine-push-service` source contract (data-only FCM,
lowercase five-value `type`, `senderPubkey`):

- **Follow & mention pushes no longer dead-end.** `parseFcmPayload` dropped any
  payload without a `referencedEventId`; follows/mentions have none. Now
  `senderPubkey` + `eventId` are parsed and carried through the
  local-notification payload and `NotificationTapEvent`, and the push executor
  routes follows to the actor profile (and unresolvable targets to
  profile/inbox) instead of silently returning.
- **Comment auto-open unified.** The push path keyed auto-open off a `'reply'`
  string the service never sends (it sends lowercase `'comment'`), so push
  comments never auto-opened. Now driven by the shared
  `notificationKindOpensComments` policy.
- **Removed dead code:** `NotificationPayloadKind.reply`.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4727 (parent epic #4200)

## Out of Scope

- **#4728** — foreground local notifications still don't carry a payload
  (`handleForegroundMessage` → `sendLocal` drops it). This PR establishes the
  contract they'll feed; #4728 wires the foreground producer onto it.
- **#4730** — `referencedDTag` owned-video attribution safety.
- Converging the in-app vs push video *screen* (`PooledFullscreenVideoFeedScreen`
  vs `VideoDetailScreen`) — intentionally preserved per the issue's "preserve
  current working behaviors from the in-app path."
- Profile deep-link nav-stack push/skip parity (#4331) — the follow→profile push
  uses `push()` directly and does not depend on it.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test` → **No issues found**
- `flutter test test/notifications/ test/services/notification_service_test.dart
  test/services/notification_helpers_test.dart
  test/main_notification_tap_routing_test.dart
  test/main_video_deep_link_nav_action_test.dart` → **254 pass** (+28 new cases:
  shared decision per-kind, push routing per-kind, follow/mention payload
  parsing, follow tap-emit, anti-drift equality)
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` → clean

### Known residual
Cold-start navigator readiness for the new direct profile/inbox
`goRouterProvider` navigation is runtime-only (not statically provable);
reasoned safe because the deferred FCM startup phase fires after the widget tree
mounts — the same precondition the existing video → deep-link-stream path
already relies on.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

issue.title: DM reaction picker: the "+" (custom emoji) button is a no-op
issue.body:
## Summary

In the DM message reaction picker (long-press a message bubble), the trailing **+** button — intended to open a full emoji picker for a custom reaction — does nothing. Tapping it simply dismisses the sheet.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Inbox and enter any DM conversation.
2. Long-press a message bubble to open the reaction picker (the quick-reaction row above the Copy / Delete actions).
3. Tap the **+** button at the right end of the quick-reaction row.

**Expected:** a full emoji picker opens so you can react with any emoji beyond the six quick reactions (❤️ 😂 🔥 😮 😢 👍).

**Actual:** the sheet dismisses and nothing happens — no picker, no reaction sent.

## Root cause

The **+** button (`_MoreButton` in `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/widgets/reaction_picker_overlay.dart`) returns `ReactionPickerResult(openFullPicker: true)`, but the caller in `conversation_view.dart` (`_onMessageLongPress`) is a stub:

```dart
if (result.openFullPicker) {
  // TODO(#4633): wire full emoji_picker_flutter sheet.
  return;
}
```

The full `emoji_picker_flutter` integration was deferred when DM reactions shipped (#4633).

## Decision needed

Whether to (a) wire up the full custom emoji picker, or (b) drop the **+** affordance permanently. Until that is decided, the broken affordance should not be visible to users.

## Mitigation

A temporary fix removes the **+** button from the quick-reaction row while keeping the `openFullPicker` result field and the `conversation_view` handler as a dormant, commented integration seam, so the affordance can be restored without reshaping the result type once the decision lands. The six quick reactions are unaffected.

issue.title: feat: save and label community audio

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
### What would you like?

Allow users to save audio from other users into their own account for future reuse, similar to Instagram’s “Save Audio” behavior. Also allow users to add custom labels/tags to audio when publishing it to the community library so sounds are easier to discover (e.g. “horses hooves”, “wind blowing”, “crowd ambience”).

### How would this be useful for you?

Sound designers and Foley artists often discover useful audio while browsing other creators’ content. Being able to save audio for later would improve workflow efficiency and encourage reuse of community content. Custom labels/tags would also make audio discovery significantly easier compared to relying only on loop titles.

### When would you use this?

While browsing the community library or another creator’s profile, a user could save interesting audio into a personal collection for future projects. When uploading audio, the creator could add descriptive tags so others can find it through search or browsing.

### Anything else?

_No response_

issue.title: refactor(providers): break remaining transitive app_providers dependency cycle
issue.body:
## Summary
The upload/media extraction in PR #4550 is safe to merge, but the provider split is not fully complete yet: several already-split provider files still import app_providers.dart, leaving a transitive dependency cycle in the provider graph.

## Scope
Break the remaining back-imports so split provider files depend on leaf modules instead of the aggregator.

Current known imports:
- mobile/lib/providers/auth_providers.dart
- mobile/lib/providers/environment_provider.dart
- mobile/lib/providers/moderation_providers.dart

## Expected outcome
- Remove those app_providers.dart imports where possible.
- Move or further split the still-shared providers they depend on.
- Preserve existing external provider names and behavior.
- Keep generated files in sync.

## Context
Follow-up to PR #4550.
Related maintainability epic: #4339.

review.body: Reviewed locally. Import rewiring and helper relocation are safe; no findings.

issue.body:
## Summary
Notifications remain one of the highest-risk user-facing areas in the app. Active issues exist across unread-state correctness, row rendering, actor identity, tap-target routing, push registration reliability, and residual dual-system debt.

This issue is the coordination source of truth for notifications work this week.

## Assignee
`@Chardot`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. unread/data correctness
2. tap-target/navigation correctness
3. row rendering / actor clarity
4. push registration and cold-start delivery
5. cleanup of dual systems / residual debt

## Subgroup
- `@Chardot` — DRI
- `@dcadenas` — push / auth-readiness / cold-start delivery
- `@realmeylisdev` — unread-state and notification data consistency
- `@untreu2` — routing / service-path bugs

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a product, design, or architecture decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this parent issue as the coordination source of truth for notifications
- read linked child issues before starting implementation
- follow the execution order unless explicitly told otherwise
- avoid narrow symptom-only fixes in known weak paths
- update linked issues if dependencies or scope change

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

The expectation is:
- no temporary hacks, fragile stopgaps, or TODO-style deferrals without an explicit linked follow-up issue
- eliminate as much adjacent existing debt as possible while touching this area
- prefer fixes that move the codebase toward repository standards: explicit state-driven behavior, clear ownership boundaries, repository-appropriate abstractions, and test-backed changes
- if a short-term workaround is truly unavoidable, it must be called out explicitly in the issue and PR, with the follow-up issue linked before merge

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.

- actor identity and row rendering

- push registration and cold-start reliability
- cleanup of legacy/duplicate notification paths

- generic UI polish outside notification surfaces

## Child Issues

- `fix(notifications): complete tap-target routing for likes, comments, replies, and reposts`

issue.title: fix(notifications): eliminate duplicate push rendering after payload verification
issue.body:
## Summary
Users are seeing duplicate push banners. The likely cause is split rendering between OS-delivered notifications and the app's background/local notification path, but the exact payload combinations need to be verified and then gated safely in the client.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Parent
- #4200

## Scope
- capture and verify actual FCM/APNS payload combinations for duplicate-banner cases
- make mobile-side rendering safe when the OS has already presented the notification
- avoid introducing more duplicate-suppression state than necessary
- coordinate with any server payload changes needed in `divinevideo/divine-push-service`

## Why
This is a user-visible correctness bug in a high-risk path. The mobile app should defend itself against duplicate presentation even if the server payload regresses.

## Related User Reports
- #4708

## Dependencies
- related backend issue in `divinevideo/divine-push-service`

## Acceptance Criteria
- one incoming push produces one visible notification banner
- mobile-side gating is covered by tests for the verified payload shape(s)
- backend coordination is documented if payload changes are also required

## Done When
- duplicate banners are no longer reproducible for the verified payload cases

issue.title: fix(notifications): stop unsafe owned-video fallback in notification attribution
issue.body:
## Summary
Notification rows still have an unsafe fallback that synthesizes a recipient-owned video addressable ID from `referencedDTag` even when the owning pubkey is not authoritative. That can surface the wrong video or route to the wrong target when payload data is ambiguous or incorrect.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Parent
- #4200

## Scope
- stop using recipient-owned addressable synthesis when owner data is not authoritative
- keep `referencedEventId` as the canonical navigation source when ownership is unknown
- harden row construction against mismatched `referenced_video` metadata vs `referenced_event_id`
- add test coverage for wrong-owner / ambiguous payload cases

## Related User Reports
- #4694

## Dependencies
- related backend data-integrity work may be needed in `divinevideo/divine-push-service` or upstream notification producers
- mobile should still fail safely without waiting on backend fixes

## Acceptance Criteria
- ambiguous notification payloads do not route to another user's video
- the client avoids synthesizing recipient-owned routes without authoritative ownership data
- tests pin safe behavior for mismatched or partial payloads

## Done When
- notification navigation and row attribution no longer depend on unsafe owned-video synthesis

issue.title: fix(notifications): remove mark-all-on-leave and restore unread badge correctness
issue.body:
## Summary
Unread badge behavior is still wrong because the notifications surface marks everything read on leave via `MarkAllReadOnDispose`, while realtime and per-item read flows are expected to converge through the repository snapshot. This causes the red badge to clear too aggressively and makes the notifications UX feel unreliable.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Parent
- #4200

## Scope
- remove or replace `MarkAllReadOnDispose`
- restore explicit unread/read transitions only
- keep badge/list convergence through the repository as the single source of truth
- validate realtime unread updates and per-item read behavior

## Related User Reports
- #4708
- #4694

## Why
The notifications architecture already moved unread state into the repository and badge cubit. The current mark-all-on-leave policy fights that architecture and creates user-visible correctness bugs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- opening and leaving notifications does not automatically zero unread state
- per-item read behavior converges across the list and badge
- realtime arrivals increment unread state without waiting for a manual refresh
- tests cover badge convergence after explicit reads and after realtime arrivals

## Done When
- there is no remaining automatic mark-all-read-on-leave behavior
- unread state changes only for deliberate read transitions

issue.title: fix(notifications): preserve normalized payloads for foreground local notification taps
issue.body:
## Summary
Foreground FCM notifications currently display a local notification banner without preserving the normalized notification payload needed for tap handling. As a result, local-notification taps can still fail even if the shared routing logic is correct.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Parent
- #4200

## Scope
- ensure foreground/local notifications carry the same normalized payload shape used by the background/system-push path
- preserve `referencedEventId` and `notificationType` for local notification taps
- validate cold-start and resumed-app behavior for locally displayed notification taps
- keep the payload contract explicit and testable

## Why
This is a separate correctness gap from routing itself. Without a valid payload on local notifications, tap handling remains broken on the foreground path even after the router is unified.

## Dependencies
- pairs closely with #4727
- can ship as a narrow PR if the routing layer work is already in progress or merged

## Acceptance Criteria
- foreground FCM banners emit local notifications with the same tap payload contract as the other paths
- tapping a foreground-generated local notification deep-links correctly
- tests pin the payload shape so regressions are caught early

## Done When
- local notification taps preserve enough context for the shared router to behave correctly

issue.title: feat(dm): wire full emoji picker for custom reactions
issue.body:
## Description

The **+** button in the DM reaction long-press row was intended to open a full emoji picker, but its caller handler was a no-op stub (`TODO(#4633)`): tapping it just dismissed the sheet and did nothing (#4710). Per @hm21's review, this PR **wires it up** rather than removing it.

- Added `FullReactionEmojiPickerSheet` — a Divine dark-styled bottom sheet wrapping `pro_image_editor`'s built-in `EmojiEditor`, which is already a direct dependency for the video editor. No new picker package.
- `conversation_view._onMessageLongPress` now opens the picker on **+** and dispatches the picked emoji through the existing `ConversationReactionToggled` path (extracted a shared `_toggleReaction` helper used by both the quick row and the full picker).
- No repository or protocol work: the NIP-17 wrapped-reaction plumbing from #4633 already accepts arbitrary emoji, so a custom emoji flows through unchanged.

This supersedes the earlier "temporarily remove the **+** button" approach. Making the path live also clears the dead `openFullPicker` seam, the stale `TODO(#4633)` breadcrumbs (that issue is closed), and re-uses the previously-orphaned `dmReactionAddCustomA11yLabel` ARB key — resolving all three self-review threads by construction.

## Out of Scope

- Theming the picker's secondary bars beyond the main grid background — the package's dark defaults are used for the bottom action / search bar.
- A widget test that taps a specific emoji in the third-party grid and asserts the dispatched event: brittle across `pro_image_editor` versions. The picker-opens and dismiss→null paths are tested; the final dispatch hop reuses the (tested) quick-reaction `_toggleReaction` helper.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — **No issues found**
- `dart format <changed files>` — clean (0 changed)
- `flutter test test/screens/inbox/conversation/` — **119/119 passing**, including:
  - new `full_reaction_emoji_picker_sheet_test.dart` (picker mounts; dismiss → null)
  - strengthened `reaction_picker_overlay_test.dart` (**+** pops `openFullPicker: true`)
  - new end-to-end `conversation_view_test.dart` case (long-press → **+** → `EmojiEditor` opens)

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

**Related Issue:** Closes #4710 — completes the full-picker integration deferred by #4633

issue.title: fix(notifications): unify push, local, and in-app notification tap routing
issue.body:
## Summary
System push taps, local-notification taps, and in-app notification-row taps do not currently share one routing contract. That split has allowed follow pushes to dead-end, comments/replies to behave differently by path, and foreground/local notifications to lose navigation context.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Parent
- #4200

## Scope
- unify notification tap behavior across:
  - FCM system push taps (`getInitialMessage`, `onMessageOpenedApp`)
  - local notification taps
  - in-app notification row taps
- define one normalized notification action model / router for:
  - follow
  - like
  - repost
  - comment
  - reply
  - mention
- preserve current working behaviors from the in-app path while eliminating drift from the push path
- provide a deterministic fallback destination when a target cannot be resolved

## Why
The current code has richer branching in the in-app notifications view than in the system-push path. Foreground/local notifications are also not using the same routing contract. This leaves correctness gaps even though the notifications BLoC/repository migration is otherwise largely complete.

## Related User Reports
- #4694

## Dependencies
- coordinate with any push payload changes tracked in `divinevideo/divine-push-service`
- can begin before backend changes as long as the mobile side handles missing fields safely

## Acceptance Criteria
- tapping a follow notification from any entry path lands on a useful destination
- comment/reply notifications consistently open the correct video/comments context
- system push taps, local notification taps, and in-app row taps cannot drift because they use the same routing contract
- unknown or unresolved targets fall back safely instead of silently doing nothing

## Done When
- one shared routing path is used for all notification entry points
- tests cover each notification kind across the shared routing layer

System push taps, local-notification taps, and in-app notification-row taps do not currently share one routing contract. That split has allowed follow pushes to dead-end, comments/replies to behave differently by path, and foreground/local notifications to lose navigation context.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Parent
- #4200

## Scope
- unify notification tap behavior across:
  - FCM system push taps (`getInitialMessage`, `onMessageOpenedApp`)
  - local notification taps
  - in-app notification row taps
- define one normalized notification action model / router for:
  - follow
  - like
  - repost
  - comment
  - reply
  - mention
- preserve current working behaviors from the in-app path while eliminating drift from the push path
- provide a deterministic fallback destination when a target cannot be resolved

## Why
The current code has richer branching in the in-app notifications view than in the system-push path. Foreground/local notifications are also not using the same routing contract. This leaves correctness gaps even though the notifications BLoC/repository migration is otherwise largely complete.

## Related User Reports
- #4694

## Dependencies
- coordinate with any push payload changes tracked in `divinevideo/divine-push-service`
- can begin before backend changes as long as the mobile side handles missing fields safely

## Acceptance Criteria
- tapping a follow notification from any entry path lands on a useful destination
- comment/reply notifications consistently open the correct video/comments context
- system push taps, local notification taps, and in-app row taps cannot drift because they use the same routing contract
- unknown or unresolved targets fall back safely instead of silently doing nothing

## Done When
- one shared routing path is used for all notification entry points
- tests cover each notification kind across the shared routing layer

issue.title: feat(dm): wire full emoji picker for custom reactions
issue.body:
## Description

The **+** button in the DM reaction long-press row was intended to open a full emoji picker, but its caller handler was a no-op stub (`TODO(#4633)`): tapping it just dismissed the sheet and did nothing (#4710). Per @hm21's review, this PR **wires it up** rather than removing it.

- Added `FullReactionEmojiPickerSheet` — a Divine dark-styled bottom sheet wrapping `pro_image_editor`'s built-in `EmojiEditor`, which is already a direct dependency for the video editor. No new picker package.
- `conversation_view._onMessageLongPress` now opens the picker on **+** and dispatches the picked emoji through the existing `ConversationReactionToggled` path (extracted a shared `_toggleReaction` helper used by both the quick row and the full picker).
- No repository or protocol work: the NIP-17 wrapped-reaction plumbing from #4633 already accepts arbitrary emoji, so a custom emoji flows through unchanged.

This supersedes the earlier "temporarily remove the **+** button" approach. Making the path live also clears the dead `openFullPicker` seam, the stale `TODO(#4633)` breadcrumbs (that issue is closed), and re-uses the previously-orphaned `dmReactionAddCustomA11yLabel` ARB key — resolving all three self-review threads by construction.

## Out of Scope

- Theming the picker's secondary bars beyond the main grid background — the package's dark defaults are used for the bottom action / search bar.
- A widget test that taps a specific emoji in the third-party grid and asserts the dispatched event: brittle across `pro_image_editor` versions. The picker-opens and dismiss→null paths are tested; the final dispatch hop reuses the (tested) quick-reaction `_toggleReaction` helper.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — **No issues found**
- `dart format <changed files>` — clean (0 changed)
- `flutter test test/screens/inbox/conversation/` — **119/119 passing**, including:
  - new `full_reaction_emoji_picker_sheet_test.dart` (picker mounts; dismiss → null)
  - strengthened `reaction_picker_overlay_test.dart` (**+** pops `openFullPicker: true`)
  - new end-to-end `conversation_view_test.dart` case (long-press → **+** → `EmojiEditor` opens)

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

**Related Issue:** Closes #4710 — completes the full-picker integration deferred by #4633

@hm21 thanks for the review — all three are addressed in 92e9e7975:

1. **Categories localized** — `I18nEmojiEditor` is now built from `context.l10n`; 10 new ARB keys (9 category titles + search hint) translated across all 18 locales.

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+// ABOUTME: Full emoji picker bottom sheet for DM custom reactions. Wraps
+// ABOUTME: pro_image_editor's EmojiEditor in a Divine dark-styled sheet.
+
+import 'package:divine_ui/divine_ui.dart';
+import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
+import 'package:pro_image_editor/pro_image_editor.dart';
+
+/// Bottom sheet that lets the user pick any emoji as a DM reaction.
+///
+/// Wraps [EmojiEditor] from `pro_image_editor` — already a direct
+/// dependency for the video editor — so the full emoji set is available
+/// beyond the six quick reactions, without adding a new picker package.
+/// The picked emoji flows through the same [ConversationReactionToggled]
+/// path as a quick reaction.
+class FullReactionEmojiPickerSheet {
+  /// Visible height of the picker body, excluding the keyboard inset.
+  static const double _bodyHeight = 320;
+
+  /// Dark-mode editor configuration. Matches the picker grid background to
+  /// the surrounding sheet so the surface reads as a single dark panel.
+  static const _editorConfigs = ProImageEditorConfigs(
+    emojiEditor: EmojiEditorConfigs(
+      style: EmojiEditorStyle(
+        backgroundColor: VineTheme.surfaceBackground,
+      ),
+    ),
+  );
+
+  /// Shows the picker and resolves to the selected emoji, or `null` if the
+  /// sheet was dismissed without a choice.
+  static Future<String?> show({required BuildContext context}) async {
+    final layer = await showModalBottomSheet<EmojiLayer>(
+      context: context,
+      backgroundColor: VineTheme.surfaceBackground,
+      isScrollControlled: true,
+      shape: const RoundedRectangleBorder(
+        borderRadius: BorderRadius.vertical(
+          top: Radius.circular(VineTheme.bottomSheetBorderRadius),
+        ),
+      ),
+      builder: (sheetContext) {
+        return SafeArea(
+          top: false,
+          child: ConstrainedBox(
+            constraints: BoxConstraints(
+              maxHeight:
+                  _bodyHeight + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(sheetContext).bottom,
+            ),
+            child: const EmojiEditor(configs: _editorConfigs),
+          ),
+        );
+      },
+    );
+    return layer?.emoji;
+  }
comment.body: Done in 92e9e7975, with one deliberate tweak: I used `scrollable: false`. In the default (scrollable) mode `VineBottomSheet` places `body` inside an `Expanded`, which overrides the `ConstrainedBox(maxHeight:)` and nests `EmojiEditor`'s own scroll inside a `DraggableScrollableSheet`. Fixed mode keeps the ~320px height and avoids the nested-scroll gesture overlap, while still inheriting the Divine chrome (rounded corners, drag handle, surface color) — so I dropped the manual `backgroundColor`/`shape`/`SafeArea` and set `EmojiEditorStyle.showDragHandle: false` to avoid a double handle. Happy to switch to the draggable variant if you'd prefer it.

issue.title: chore: configure App Store Connect / Apple Developer settings for ProofSign device auth
issue.body:
We need to complete the Apple-side configuration required for the ProofSign device-auth flow described in PR #3515 before the follow-up implementation PR lands.

Context:
- PR: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3515
- Main setup comment: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3515#issuecomment-4351815647
- Follow-up note calling this out: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3515#issuecomment-4527660641

What needs to be verified or configured:
1. In Apple Developer, confirm the app identifier used by Divine has the App Attest capability enabled.
2. Confirm the app's Apple App ID value in the format TEAMID.bundleid.
3. Confirm this Apple App ID is provisioned on the ProofSign server.
4. Confirm the iOS app entitlements include com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment for the intended environment.
5. If any Apple-side values are missing, document the exact values needed for:
   - PROOFSIGN_APPLE_APP_ID
   - any related server-side Apple configuration

Notes:
- The PR comment says this may already be configured, so this issue is partly verification and partly setup if anything is missing.
- App Attest only works on physical iOS devices signed into iCloud, so this should be validated against a real device flow, not Simulator.

Acceptance criteria:
- Apple-side App Attest capability is confirmed enabled for the correct app identifier.
- The correct TEAMID.bundleid value is documented.
- ProofSign server provisioning is confirmed to match that value.
- Any missing env var or entitlement requirements are documented for the follow-up PR.

issue.title: fix(images): cancel orphaned thumbnail downloads
issue.body:
Closes #4692
Closes #4696

## Summary
- replace the last cached_network_image usage with a repo-owned MediaCacheImageProvider backed by MediaCacheManager.cacheFileCancellable
- cancel in-flight thumbnail downloads when the last image listener is removed while preserving VineCachedImage's public API
- drop the cached_network_image dependency and refresh regression coverage around avatars, thumbnails, and concurrent image loading

## Verification

- flutter test --no-pub test/notifications/widgets/notification_avatar_stack_test.dart
- flutter test --no-pub test/widgets/ios_network_image_deadlock_test.dart
- flutter test --no-pub test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart
- flutter test --no-pub test/widgets/user_avatar_svg_test.dart
- flutter analyze --no-pub lib/widgets/vine_cached_image.dart packages/media_cache/lib/src/media_cache_image_provider.dart packages/media_cache/test/src/media_cache_image_provider_test.dart test/widgets/ios_network_image_deadlock_test.dart test/widgets/video_thumbnail_widget_test.dart test/widgets/comprehensive_user_avatar_test.dart test/notifications/widgets/notification_avatar_stack_test.dart test/widgets/vine_cached_image_test.dart test/widgets/profile/profile_tab_thumbnail_test.dart

## Notes
- full-repo flutter analyze still reports pre-existing infos in unrelated manual/integration scripts outside this diff; the changed files above analyze cleanly
- flutter test / flutter analyze without --no-pub can crash in this worktree because Flutter tries to delete ios/Flutter/ephemeral/Packages/.packages; verification used the already-resolved dependency graph to avoid that tooling bug

review.body: Thanks for chasing the expired-session publish-flow race. I traced the fix and I don't think this is ready to merge yet. The main blockers are: (1) the new publish-success pluralization is implemented with Dart branching instead of a single ICU plural key, (2) the new upload-success buffering state machine in `_UploadFailureListener` still has no direct tests, and (3) `isRefreshInProgress` adds unused API surface. I also left two cleanup comments on l10n lookup and new widget-test assertions because they introduce avoidable debt in the same diff.

comment.body: These new widget-test assertions hardcode English UI copy. `.claude/rules/localization.md` says widget tests should resolve strings from `AppLocalizations` instead so the test tracks the actual l10n key instead of a literal. Please update these new assertions here and in the sibling settings test.

Please avoid pulling l10n through `NavigatorKeys.root.currentContext`. The repo localization rule explicitly says not to fetch l10n through navigator-key context workarounds. This helper already takes a `BuildContext`; use that context for l10n or thread the resolved string in.

This new state machine is the riskiest part of the patch, but the PR still doesn't add any direct tests for it. Please add coverage for at least: success while authenticated, success buffered while unauthenticated then flushed on re-auth, and a vanished failed upload not being miscounted as success.

This should not branch on `count` in Dart. `.claude/rules/localization.md` requires ICU plural syntax in ARB files for plurals. Please collapse `uploadPublishedMessage` / `uploadPublishedMultipleMessage` into a single pluralized l10n key and call that here.

`isRefreshInProgress` looks unused in this PR and I couldn't find any repo callers for it. This adds speculative API surface without a current need. Please delete the getter and doc unless this revision is going to consume it somewhere concrete.

review.body: Removing the legacy bare-string fallback is fine, but this change also removes the only defensive parsing around the local-notification tap payload. Right now malformed JSON, a non-object JSON value, or a non-string `referencedEventId` will throw out of `_handleNotificationTapPayload` and flow into the app-wide Flutter error path. Please keep the legacy behavior removed, but make malformed payloads fail closed with a warning log + early return, and add replacement tests for the invalid-payload cases so this boundary stays hardened.

comment.body: Removing the legacy-path test is fine, but this PR should replace it with coverage for the new intended behavior at this parsing boundary. Please add tests that assert malformed payloads do not emit and do not throw, at minimum for: non-JSON payload, JSON that is not an object, and object payloads whose `referencedEventId` is not a string.

This turns a dormant compatibility cleanup into a new uncaught-error path. `jsonDecode(payload) as Map<String, dynamic>` and the following casts can now throw on malformed JSON, non-object JSON, or wrong-shape data, and taps route straight through this method from the plugin callback. I would still remove the legacy bare-string semantics, but keep defensive parsing here: log a warning and return on malformed payloads instead of letting the tap throw.

issue.title: fix(dm): make conversation composer send button accessible
issue.body:
## Summary
The DM conversation composer send control is visually present and tappable, but it is implemented as a bare `GestureDetector` around a decorative container with no dedicated semantic label. Screen readers do not get a clear, action-oriented announcement for the control, which leaves the composer below the repo standard already used in adjacent input components.

This was identified while reviewing PR #4709, which correctly introduced multiline composition behavior but left this pre-existing accessibility gap in place.

## Environment
- Area: `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/widgets/message_input_bar.dart`
- Affected surface: DM conversation composer
- Platforms: iOS and Android
- Assistive tech impact: VoiceOver / TalkBack users

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a DM conversation.
2. Enter any non-whitespace text so the send button becomes visible.
3. Navigate to the send control using a screen reader.
4. Listen to how the control is announced.

## Actual Result
The send affordance does not expose a DM-specific semantic label, because the control is built from a raw gesture target instead of a semantic button with an explicit accessibility string.

## Expected Result
The send affordance should be announced as a button with a clear localized label, for example `Send message`, while preserving the existing visual design and tap behavior.

## Regression?
No. This is pre-existing debt surfaced during review of #4709.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The DM composer send control exposes button semantics.
- The control has a localized screen-reader label appropriate for DM sending.
- Existing send behavior remains unchanged.
- Widget coverage verifies the semantics label so the issue does not regress.

## Proposed Fix
- Add a DM-specific localized label, e.g. `dmMessageSendLabel`.
- Wrap the control in `Semantics(button: true, ...)`.
- Replace the raw tap target with an `IconButton` or equivalent semantic button while preserving current layout and visuals.
- Add a widget test that asserts the accessibility label is present when the send button is shown.

## Links
- Source PR reviewed: #4709
- Follow-up fix PR: #4722

issue.title: Refactor inline video comment player styling ownership
issue.body:
## Summary
The rounded-corner regression from PR #4706 was fixed in the right user-facing place, but the implementation left a small ownership issue behind. `CommentItem` became responsible for restoring the inline player's rounded corners, while `VideoCommentPlayer` remained unaware of that styling contract.

## Why this should be cleaned up
- The visual contract belongs to the player component, not just one parent usage site.
- The regression test added in PR #4706 asserted a `ClipRRect` wrapper in `CommentItem`, which couples the test to one parent implementation detail instead of protecting the player API.
- Leaving the styling responsibility outside the player makes future reuse easier to get wrong and invites duplicate wrappers in other call sites.

## Cleanup
- Add an optional border-radius API to `VideoCommentPlayer`.
- Pass the radius from `CommentItem` through that API instead of wrapping the player externally.
- Move the rounded-corner regression coverage to the player test, and leave `CommentItem` testing only the wiring.

## Standard
This follow-up is needed to keep the no-new-tech-debt standard intact after PR #4706.
